title: Ozone and moisture slope differences between blackberry and milkweed did not repeat in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We compared recorded ozone injury fractions for blackberry and milkweed scored at the same forest sites in the same years. Four eastern US region-period samples had 1,504 paired site-years in 1994-2010. Models used site and year effects, annual ozone and moisture deviations, site-mean terms, weather, visit day and plant counts. Joint slope differences were +10.36, +0.16, -15.82 and -0.33 injury percentage points per 10 ppm-h ozone per moisture standard deviation. Only the early North Central four-test interval was below zero. That result used five state clusters and was uncertain with state-only errors, closer monitors or before-visit exposures. The species contrast did not repeat. This does not show equal responses or absence of damage. Species-specific scoring, selected plants, coarse exposures, survey timing and few clusters limit inference. We reuse one published archive; the samples are not independent experiments. Original code, aggregate outputs, source hashes, numerical checks and a figure are included. Source records remain outside the signed publication.

display.caption: Blackberry minus milkweed slope for the product of annual ozone and moisture deviations. Grey bars give four-test intervals. Blue bars give 95 percent two-way cluster intervals. Brown bars give state-only 95 percent intervals. The early North Central result is sensitive to the covariance estimate.

citations.reason: Exact verified panel and species-year counts; source records fully overlap. The source preserves raw retrieval code and hashes.
Prior fixed species-set audit motivates a direct paired species comparison. No code was copied.
Prior injury-history test guided the choice of a distinct question.
